findings.title: All-null serviceLevelAgreements object renders invalid SQL, so every getThreads call without SLA filters fails
findings.failure: The op always sends serviceLevelAgreements: { statuses: $slaStatuses, types: $slaTypes }. When the agent leaves both null (the default, i.e. nearly every getThreads call, filtered by status/assignee/etc. or not), ThreadsFilter zod parses it into a non-null object { types: null, statuses: null, updatedAt: null }. At the top level the DB builder returns an EMPTY fragment for it, and buildFilters only drops nulls, not empty fragments, then joins with ' AND '. The WHERE clause becomes '... AND (1 = 1 AND )' (createdAt all-null renders '1 = 1'), so Postgres throws a syntax error, threadDb.getThreads returns Err, and the MCP getThreads tool (plus its totalCount query) returns a GraphQL internal error for every customer. The PR's claim that an all-null object is a no-op only holds for the nested EXISTS path, not the top-level path the MCP query takes.
findings.fix: Fix the backend before (or together with) shipping this op, as the core API and MCP server deploy separately: in packages/aggregates/src/thread/threadDbFilterUtils.ts:946 and :979 return rdsDbUtils.filtering.ignoreFilter() (packages/db/src/filtering.ts:10, the helper rangeFilter already uses for its all-null case) instead of sql.fragment``, or collapse an all-null object to null in packages/core-graphql/src/threads/threadsFilter.ts:58. Add a litest in lambdas/core-graphql-api/src/threads/threadsQueryFilters.slas.litest.ts that runs threads with serviceLevelAgreements: {} and with { statuses: null, types: null }. Do not merge the op until that passes.
findings.evidence: threadsFilter.ts:58-72 parses the object to non-null with null defaults. determineThreadFilters.ts:179-180 spreads it through unchanged. threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943-947 returns sql.fragment`` when statuses/types/updatedAt are all null. packages/db/src/filtering.ts:114-124 is compact(...) and then sql.join(parts, ' AND '), and lodash compact keeps the truthy empty token. threadDbFilterUtils.ts:1238-1242 and 1278-1281 wrap that as '(… AND …)'. threadDb.ts:1252 and 1357 emit 'WHERE t.workspace_id = … AND ${scopeFilter} AND ${filters}'. I ran slonik 45.5.0 from the repo (packages/db/node_modules/slonik): sql.join([fragment`1 = 1`, fragment``], fragment` AND `) prints '1 = 1 AND ', so the filter becomes '(1 = 1 AND )'. No unit or litest covers the all-null top-level case (threadDbFilterUtils.test.ts:850-950 only exercises non-null fields). The only other caller, agent-sandbox threadOps.ts:271-275, sets the object only when slaStatus is defined, so this PR is the first production caller to send it all-null. The nested path guards correctly (threadDbFilterUtils.ts:647-685) but is used only inside and/or/not.

findings.title: SLA status union selection copied 12 times across three operations
findings.failure: The same 44 line ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail selection is pasted for each of the 4 targets in each of the 3 files. A future schema change to one detail type (e.g. a new field or union member) has to be made in 12 places, and missing one lets the tools drift apart quietly.
findings.fix: Define one in-file fragment per operation, e.g. fragment GetThreadsSlaStatusDetail on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail { __typename ... on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending {...} ... }, and spread it under each target. Prefix the name per file as the broadcast ops do.
findings.evidence: The existing pattern is in-file, file-prefixed fragments in MCP ops: createBroadcast.graphql:75 and :118-175 (CreateBroadcastFilterFields etc.) and createBroadcastAudience.graphql:41 and :70-108. Duplicate blocks start at getThreadDetails.graphql:96, getThreads.graphql:174 and searchThreads.graphql:114.

checked_fine: Schema already exposes everything selected: Thread.serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary (schema.ts:13932), the 6 detail types and their fields (schema.ts:14072-14125) and ThreadsFilter.serviceLevelAgreements with ServiceLevelAgreementFilter.types/statuses (schema.ts:6564, 6624-6628). The MCP server fetches the full printed schema at container start (entrypoint.sh:23, graphql-schema/src/schemaSdlResponse.ts), so there is no deploy ordering issue for the selection sets.
Variable types match the schema: [ServiceLevelAgreementStatus!] and [ServiceLevelAgreementType!], and the enum values in the getThreads comment match schema.ts:6617-6622 and 14057-14070.
Union resolveType covers all 6 tracker statuses (resolvers.ts:11918-11935), and the field resolvers map breachTime/completedAt/cancelledAt correctly (resolvers.ts:9427-9458).

No N+1: the summary resolver short circuits when there is no tier and no policy (resolvers.ts:7761-7768), otherwise it uses serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDataLoader (serviceLevelAgreementStatusResolver.ts:15), so the 50-row searchThreads page is batched.
Selections are inserted at the Thread level in all three ops (getThreadDetails.graphql:96, getThreads.graphql:174 under edges.node, searchThreads.graphql:114 under node.thread).
The searchThreads filters are unchanged, so the SQL issue does not affect searchThreads. getThreadDetails takes no filter.
No SLA join is added for filtering, so requiresDistinct and row multiplication are unchanged (threadDbFilterUtils.ts:177-182).
Rollback is just redeploying the previous MCP image. There is no data or schema migration.
